Neurological & SpecialService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Neurological Physiotherapy ?

Neurological physiotherapy is a dedicated discipline focusing on assessing and treating individuals who experience movement, balance, and postural disorders arising from damage to the central or peripheral nervous system. Conditions such as Parkinson's disease, Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS), Multiple Sclerosis (MS), peripheral neuropathies, and traumatic brain injuries can severely compromise mobility, gait rhythm, and independence. At Dr Hamid’s Physio and Pain Clinic in Manikonda, Hyderabad, Dr. Mohammed Hamid Ali delivers structured neuro-rehabilitation aimed at retraining motor coordination, preventing falls, and maintaining high functional capacity.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

Neurological physiotherapy uses evidence-based motor learning principles and sensory cueing. For Parkinson's patients, Dr. Mohammed Hamid Ali employs high-amplitude movement training (LSVT BIG concepts), visual floor cues, and auditory metronome pacing to overcome bradykinesia. For peripheral neuropathies, balance retraining and sensory compensatory strategies restore confident, safe walking.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Neurodegenerative disorders such as Parkinson's disease leading to dopamine depletion and motor rigidity

- Peripheral neuropathies (diabetic, alcoholic, or idiopathic) causing sensory ataxia and muscle weakness

- Autoimmune demyelinating conditions including Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS) and Multiple Sclerosis (MS)

- Traumatic brain injuries (TBI) and post-concussion balance and coordination syndromes

- Spinal cord lesions, compressive myelopathies, and motor neuron disease

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Resting tremors, muscle rigidity ('cogwheel rigidity'), and bradykinesia (slowness of movement)

- Festinating, shuffling gait with short steps and tendency to lean forward (propulsion)

- Freezing of gait (FOG) when attempting to turn, start walking, or pass through doorways

- Impaired postural reflexes leading to frequent domestic falls and unsteadiness

- Peripheral numbness, burning, and loss of proprioceptive position sense in the feet

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS) motor examination criteria

2

Comprehensive sensory testing (light touch, pinprick, vibration sense, joint position sense)

3

Dynamic Gait Index (DGI) and Functional Reach Test evaluating balance stability

4

Evaluation of muscle tone, spasticity vs rigidity, and coordination (finger-to-nose, heel-to-shin)

5

Assessment of home safety, transfer capabilities, and assistive device requirements

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Large-amplitude, exaggerated movement drills to counteract Parkinsonian hypokinesia

Visual and auditory rhythmic cueing to eliminate gait freezing and normalize stride length

Intensive balance, dual-tasking, and agility exercises to prevent falls

Strengthening of anti-gravity postural muscles (quadriceps, gluteals, spinal extensors)

Energy conservation techniques and adaptive equipment recommendations

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Practice large, deliberate steps and high knee lifts when walking at home

- Use tape markers on the floor in doorways if gait freezing occurs

- Perform daily seated and standing balance exercises near a sturdy table for safety

- Ensure bathroom and corridors have bright lighting and non-skid flooring

- Maintain a regular daily schedule for medications and physiotherapy exercises

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Schedule an assessment as soon as you notice changes in your walking rhythm, frequent balance loss, progressive stiffness, or hand tremors.
Schedule Assessment Today

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Orthotics and Insole Assessment ?

Orthotics and insoles are devices placed inside footwear to change support, cushioning, or pressure distribution. They may be considered for some people with foot symptoms, but they are not needed by everyone and do not replace an assessment of the cause of pain. At the clinic, a physiotherapy assessment can review your symptoms, activity, footwear, and foot function, then discuss whether an insole or orthotic option may be worth considering. Please call ahead to confirm whether a particular product or custom fitting service is available.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

The physiotherapist reviews your history, symptoms, walking and standing tolerance, footwear, and relevant foot and ankle movement. Together, you can discuss practical options such as changing footwear, trying an off-the-shelf insole, or asking a suitable orthotics provider about a custom device. Exercise, activity changes, and other care may also be appropriate depending on assessment findings.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Foot or heel discomfort that changes with footwear or standing time

- Recurring plantar heel pain or arch discomfort

- Foot symptoms that limit walking, work, or exercise

- A need to review footwear support during a broader rehabilitation plan

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Heel, arch, or forefoot discomfort during walking or prolonged standing

- Symptoms that vary between different shoes or surfaces

- Reduced comfort during work, exercise, or daily activities

Review footwear and the activities or surfaces that affect symptoms

3

Assess relevant foot and ankle movement, strength, and functional tasks

4

Discuss appropriate next steps, including whether an orthotics referral may be useful

Individual footwear and activity guidance based on assessment

A broader exercise or rehabilitation plan when clinically appropriate

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

- Bring the shoes you use most often to your assessment

- Note which activities and surfaces make symptoms better or worse

- If trying an insole, follow fitting guidance and stop using it if it causes significant new discomfort

- Seek medical advice for severe, sudden, or unexplained foot pain

# Paediatric Physiotherapy & Child Physical Therapy in Manikonda, Hyderabad

Specialized, child-friendly physiotherapy fostering motor milestone achievement, postural alignment, and physical confidence in infants, children, and adolescents.

Call +91 76010 26596 Chat on WhatsApp

📍 Opp: HDFC Bank ATM, near Friends Colony Park, Puppalguda, Manikonda. Contact the clinic to ask about appointment availability.

![Paediatric physiotherapy and child developmental therapy in Manikonda](https://www.drhamidphysio.in/images/services/exercise-therapy.webp)

Sports, Post-Op & GeneralService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Paediatric Physiotherapy ?

Paediatric physiotherapy is the specialized clinical practice dedicated to optimizing physical development, motor milestone acquisition, posture, and musculoskeletal function in children from infancy through adolescence. Young bodies are continuously growing, with developing skeletal physis, developing neurological coordination, and unique biomechanics. Common childhood physical challenges seen at our Manikonda clinic include gross motor developmental delays (delayed crawling, standing, or walking), idiopathic toe walking, congenital torticollis, flat feet (pes planus), knock knees (genu valgum), and adolescent postural deviations (kyphosis and scoliosis). Dr. Hamid's paediatric care blends evidence-based pediatric biomechanics with playful, engaging exercises that children genuinely enjoy.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

Paediatric physiotherapy taps into the incredible neuroplasticity and adaptability of a growing child. By structuring therapeutic movements into enjoyable games, obstacle courses, and balance challenges, Dr. Mohammed Hamid Ali promotes motor coordination without inducing fear or boredom. Physiotherapy gently normalizes muscle tone, corrects joint alignment, enhances core stability, and provides parents with actionable handling strategies that nurture healthy physical development at home.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Developmental coordination delays and hypotonia (low muscle tone) affecting milestone progression

- Congenital muscular tightness, such as sternocleidomastoid contracture in infant torticollis

- Persistent primitive reflexes and sensory-seeking motor habits causing habitual toe walking

- Ligamentous hypermobility leading to excessive joint laxity, flat feet, and clumsy running gait

- Excessive modern screen time and heavy school backpacks causing early adolescent postural kyphosis

- Growth spurts and sports-related traction apophysitis (e.g. Osgood-Schlatter or Sever's disease)

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Delays in sitting, crawling, or independent walking compared to established developmental milestones

- Consistently walking on tiptoes without heel strike past the age of 2 years

- Frequent clumsiness, tripping over feet, or reluctance to engage in physical playground play

- Head tilt to one side with difficulty turning the neck fully during infant feeding or sleeping

- Complaints of growing pains, heel ache, or knee pain after playing sports or running at school

- Rounded shoulders, forward head poke, and slouching postures during homework and screen use

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Developmental motor milestone screening benchmarked against age-appropriate gross motor scales

2

Observational gait analysis assessing foot strike, pelvic tilt, knee tracking, and arm swing

3

Musculoskeletal evaluation of joint flexibility, ligamentous laxity (Beighton score), and bone alignment

4

Muscle tone and motor strength assessment across major postural muscle groups

5

Comprehensive consultation with parents regarding birth history, daily habits, and family observations

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Play-based motor retraining utilizing gym balls, stepping stones, and dynamic balance courses

Gentle manual passive stretching and myofascial elongation for tight muscle groups (calf, neck)

Core stability exercises strengthening abdominal, gluteal, and back postural musculature

Sensory-motor integration drills to encourage proper heel-toe walking mechanics

Customized parental home exercise guidance and footwear recommendations for growing feet

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Incorporate daily active tummy time for infants to build vital neck and shoulder girdle strength

- Encourage barefoot play on diverse natural surfaces (grass, sand, carpet) to stimulate foot arch development

- Limit continuous sedentary tablet and phone screen time; encourage active outdoor playground games

- Ensure your child's school backpack does not exceed 10% to 15% of their total body weight

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Schedule an assessment if your child has not started walking independently by 15-18 months, persistently walks on their tiptoes, exhibits a consistent head tilt, complains of recurrent leg pains, or shows noticeable asymmetry in limb movement.
Schedule Assessment Today

# Patellar Tracking Disorder Physiotherapy in Manikonda, Hyderabad

Specialized clinical rehabilitation for abnormal kneecap tracking, patellar malalignment, and anterior knee dysfunction.

Call +91 76010 26596 Chat on WhatsApp

📍 Opp: HDFC Bank ATM, near Friends Colony Park, Puppalguda, Manikonda. Contact the clinic to ask about appointment availability.

![Patellar tracking disorder physiotherapy and kneecap alignment treatment in Manikonda clinic](https://www.drhamidphysio.in/images/services/condition-knee-pain.webp)

KneeService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Patellar Tracking Disorder Physiotherapy ?

Pain around the kneecap can occur with activity and may have different contributing factors. Kneecap movement is only one part of an assessment; symptoms do not establish a specific structural problem by themselves. A clinician can discuss whether physiotherapy may be appropriate.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

An assessment may consider knee, hip, and foot movement, activity, symptoms, and goals. If appropriate, a plan may include exercise or other options. Taping may offer short-term support for some people, but response varies and it does not guarantee lasting correction.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Weakness in the vastus medialis obliquus (VMO) failing to counteract lateral pull

- Tightness in the lateral retinaculum, ITB, or vastus lateralis pulling the patella outward

- Structural factors including high Q-angle (common in women), shallow trochlear groove, or patella alta

- Hip abductor weakness causing dynamic knee valgus and internal tibial rotation

- Poor foot mechanics with overpronation increasing tibial internal rotation

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Pain in the front of the knee, particularly when climbing stairs, squatting, or standing from sitting

- Sensation of the kneecap catching, grinding, or popping during knee movement

- Feeling that the kneecap is unstable, slipping, or may dislocate

- Pain when sitting with bent knees for prolonged periods

- Visible lateral shifting of the patella when extending the knee

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Patellar tracking observation during active knee extension in sitting and standing

2

Patellar glide, tilt, and rotation mobility assessment

3

Q-angle measurement and lower limb alignment analysis

4

VMO activation timing testing and comparison with vastus lateralis

5

Single-leg squat analysis for dynamic knee valgus and hip control

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Patellar mobilization to release tight lateral retinaculum and improve medial glide

Patellar taping may be considered where appropriate; response varies

Isolated VMO strengthening exercises (inner range quads, terminal knee extension)

Hip abductor and external rotator strengthening to control femoral rotation

ITB and lateral structure stretching with foam rolling and specific stretches

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Perform VMO activation exercises (straight leg raises with foot externally rotated) 3 times daily

- Apply ice for 15 minutes after activities that provoke knee pain

- Avoid deep squats and lunges until tracking is corrected and pain-free

- Use patellar taping as taught by Dr. Hamid during aggravating activities

- Stretch the ITB and hip flexors daily to reduce lateral tension on the patella

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Seek assessment if you experience persistent front-of-knee pain, grinding sensations, or feelings of kneecap instability. Early treatment prevents cartilage damage and progression to arthritis.
Schedule Assessment Today

# PCL Injury Physiotherapy in Manikonda, Hyderabad

Specialized clinical rehabilitation for posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) sprains, dashboard injuries, and posterior knee instability.

Call +91 76010 26596 Chat on WhatsApp

📍 Opp: HDFC Bank ATM, near Friends Colony Park, Puppalguda, Manikonda. Contact the clinic to ask about appointment availability.

![PCL injury physiotherapy and posterior knee stability in Manikonda](https://www.drhamidphysio.in/images/services/condition-sports-injury.webp)

KneeService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is PCL Injury Physiotherapy ?

The Posterior Cruciate Ligament (PCL) is the strongest ligament in the knee joint, preventing backward translation of the tibia on the femur. PCL injuries occur less frequently than ACL tears and are commonly caused by high-energy trauma — such as a bent knee striking a car dashboard in a traffic collision, or falling heavily directly onto a flexed knee with the foot pointed downward. Fortunately, isolated Grade I and II PCL tears have tremendous intrinsic healing capacity. At Dr Hamid’s Physio and Pain Clinic in Manikonda, Hyderabad, we provide specialized conservative rehabilitation focused on aggressive quadriceps dynamic stabilization.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

Unlike the ACL, where hamstrings act as agonists, in PCL rehabilitation the quadriceps is the primary muscular stabilizer that pulls the tibia forward, counteracting posterior sag. Dr. Mohammed Hamid Ali prescribes intensive quadriceps strengthening, strict posterior tibial support, and gradual range of motion restoration while temporarily limiting open-chain hamstring contractions that would pull the healing ligament backward.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Direct blow to the anterior upper shin while the knee is bent (e.g. car dashboard collision)

- Falling hard onto a fully bent knee during football, kabaddi, or outdoor sports

- Violent hyperextension injury to the knee during an athletic tackle or misstep

- Sudden extreme rotational force combined with posterior tibial translation

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Vague, deep posterior knee aching and fullness behind the knee joint

- Posterior 'sag' of the tibia when resting with knees bent at 90 degrees

- Mild to moderate swelling and tenderness in the popliteal fossa

- Instability or difficulty walking down declines, ramps, or stairs

- Pain during deep knee flexion (squatting, kneeling, sitting cross-legged)

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Posterior Drawer test at 90 degrees of knee flexion to grade posterior laxity

2

Godfrey's test (posterior sag sign) evaluated with hips and knees at 90 degrees

3

Quadriceps active test to evaluate dynamic anterior reduction of the displaced tibia

4

Dial test at 30 and 90 degrees to rule out associated posterolateral corner (PLC) injury

5

Evaluation of extension and flexion limits in accordance with ligament healing phase

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Application and management of posterior dynamic PCL braces in early recovery

Strict avoidance of active isolated hamstring contractions during the initial 6 weeks

Aggressive quadriceps strengthening (straight leg raises, terminal knee extensions, leg press)

Progressive knee flexion mobilization under controlled anterior tibial support

Advanced balance, proprioception, and functional athletic retraining

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Wear your dynamic PCL brace with posterior tibial pad support as instructed

- Do not perform active hamstring curls or pull your heel back during early recovery

- Perform quadriceps setting exercises and straight leg raises multiple times daily

- Avoid deep kneeling or sitting on your heels until cleared by Dr. Hamid

- Apply ice packs to the back of the knee following exercise sessions

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Schedule an assessment promptly if you have experienced a direct blow to your shin, notice a backward sag in your knee, or have difficulty walking down slopes.
Schedule Assessment Today

# Plantar Fasciitis Physiotherapy in Manikonda, Hyderabad

Specialized clinical rehabilitation for plantar fasciitis, arch pain, Windlass mechanism dysfunction, and plantar aponeurosis strain.

Call +91 76010 26596 Chat on WhatsApp

📍 Opp: HDFC Bank ATM, near Friends Colony Park, Puppalguda, Manikonda. Contact the clinic to ask about appointment availability.

![Plantar fasciitis physiotherapy and arch pain treatment in Manikonda clinic](https://www.drhamidphysio.in/images/services/foot-and-ankle-care.svg)

Other Joints & PainService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Plantar Fasciitis Physiotherapy ?

Plantar heel pain can involve the band of tissue under the foot, though other causes are possible. Pain is often noticed with standing or walking. Assessment may help discuss activity, exercise, footwear, or other care options that suit the individual.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

Research shows that plantar fasciitis responds exceptionally well to mechanical loading and tissue mobilization. Dr. Mohammed Hamid Ali combines specific plantar fascia stretching, the proven Rathleff high-load strength protocol, gastrocnemius-soleus soft tissue release, and low-dye arch taping. This stimulates collagen remodelling and restores the foot's natural Windlass mechanism.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Severe calf and Achilles tendon tightness limiting ankle dorsiflexion and overloading the arch

- Overpronation (flat feet) causing excessive tensile strain on the medial plantar fascia

- High rigid foot arches (pes cavus) with poor shock-absorption capacity

- Prolonged standing on hard concrete or tiled floors in retail, teaching, healthcare, or corporate roles

- Sudden increases in running or walking mileage in improper footwear

- Elevated body weight increasing cyclic mechanical load on the plantar fascia

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Stabbing, intense pain under the medial heel with the very first steps in the morning

- Pain that flares up after prolonged periods of sitting or rest when standing up

- Deep aching along the medial arch of the foot after prolonged standing or walking

- Tenderness when pressing directly on the inner underside of the heel bone

- Limping or walking on the toes or outer edge of the foot to avoid putting weight on the heel

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Windlass test: Passive dorsiflexion of the first metatarsophalangeal (MTP) joint to reproduce pain

2

Palpation of the medial calcaneal tubercle and entire central band of the plantar fascia

3

Weight-bearing ankle dorsiflexion lunge test to quantify calf muscle tightness

4

Foot Posture Index (FPI-6) assessment to categorize foot arch mechanics

5

Gait assessment evaluating midfoot pronation and propulsion during toe-off

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Plantafascia-specific stretching (pulling toes back toward shin while palpating the taut band)

High-load strength training (calf raises with a rolled towel under the big toe to engage the Windlass mechanism)

Myofascial trigger point release and instrument-assisted mobilization for the calf and soleus

Foot taping may be considered as temporary support if appropriate; response varies

Prescription of custom arch-support orthotics and night splint guidance

Recovery and progress

The time to improvement varies with the cause, symptom duration, activity, and chosen plan. Follow-up can help review comfort and function and adjust activity or exercise as needed.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Perform the big-toe extension plantar stretch for 3 sets of 10 repetitions before standing out of bed

- Never walk barefoot on tiled or concrete surfaces; use supportive orthotic slippers at home

- Perform progressive heel raises with a towel under your toes as prescribed by Dr. Hamid

- Roll your foot over a cold or frozen water bottle for 10 minutes every evening

- Wear supportive shoes with a slight heel raise (10-15 mm) to offload the Achilles and plantar fascia

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Schedule an assessment if you experience stabbing morning heel pain, difficulty standing at work, or arch soreness that doesn't improve with rest.
Schedule Assessment Today

Sports, Post-Op & GeneralService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Post Hip Replacement Rehabilitation ?

Rehabilitation after hip replacement may support movement, strength, walking, and daily activities. The plan depends on the operation, the person's health and progress, and the surgeon's advice. Follow any approach-specific precautions provided by the treating team; physiotherapy does not guarantee a particular outcome.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

Rehabilitation after hip replacement may include movement practice, strength exercises, walking, and daily-activity training, while following the surgeon's instructions. The plan and pace should reflect the procedure, health, symptoms, and individual progress. No particular outcome can be promised.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Post-surgical muscle weakness, particularly in gluteal and hip abductor muscles

- Altered gait patterns developed during years of pre-operative hip arthritis

- Hip joint stiffness and soft tissue contracture from surgical healing

- Balance deficits and fear of falling during early weight-bearing

- Need for strict adherence to hip precautions (posterior approach) to prevent dislocation

- Muscle atrophy from pre-operative pain avoidance and limited mobility

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Difficulty walking without a walker, crutches, or cane

- Weakness when lifting the leg or standing from a chair

- Stiffness and limited hip range of motion

- Apprehension about hip movement and weight-bearing

- Struggling with stairs, getting in and out of bed, or car transfers

- Persistent swelling or discomfort around the surgical site

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Review of surgical approach (posterior, anterior, lateral) and specific precautions

2

Hip range of motion measurement within safe limits

3

Hip abductor and extensor strength testing

4

Gait analysis with assistive device assessment

5

Functional transfer assessment (bed, chair, toilet, car)

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Follow the surgeon's approach-specific precautions and weight-bearing instructions

Progress movement, strength, and walking practice in line with symptoms and the treating team's advice

Build daily-activity skills and balance when appropriate for the person's recovery

Discuss progression toward recreational activity with the treating team

Functional training for daily activities (dressing, bathing, transfers)

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Strictly follow hip precautions: no bending past 90 degrees, no crossing legs, no twisting the operated leg inward

- Use elevated toilet seat and chair/armchair risers as recommended

- Sleep with a pillow between your legs (if instructed by your surgeon)

- Perform prescribed ankle pumps and gentle hip exercises daily

- Apply ice packs for 15-20 minutes after activities to reduce swelling

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Follow the surgeon's instructions about when to start rehabilitation and which precautions apply. Contact the treating team if pain, swelling, wound changes, or mobility concerns worsen.
Schedule Assessment Today

# Post Knee Replacement Rehabilitation in Manikonda, Hyderabad

Sports, Post-Op & GeneralService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Post Knee Replacement Rehabilitation ?

Rehabilitation after knee replacement may support movement, strength, walking, and daily activities. The plan depends on the operation, the person's health and progress, and the surgeon's advice. Physiotherapy does not guarantee a particular outcome.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

Rehabilitation after knee replacement may include movement practice, strength exercises, walking and daily-activity training, following the surgeon's instructions. The plan and pace should reflect the procedure, health, symptoms, and progress of the individual. No particular range of motion or outcome can be promised.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Post-surgical joint stiffness and capsular contracture from tissue healing

- Quadriceps inhibition and weakness following surgical trauma

- Persistent post-operative swelling and joint effusion

- Altered gait patterns developed during years of pre-operative arthritis

- Scar tissue formation requiring manual mobilization

- Muscle atrophy from pre-operative pain avoidance and disuse

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Significant stiffness and inability to fully bend or straighten the knee

- Weakness when attempting to lift the leg straight (extension lag)

- Difficulty walking without a walker, crutches, or cane

- Persistent swelling around the knee and lower leg

- Pain and apprehension during weight-bearing activities

- Struggling with stairs, getting in and out of chairs, or car transfers

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Goniometric measurement of knee flexion and extension range of motion

2

Assessment of active extension lag and quadriceps activation

3

Circumferential measurement of swelling and calf circumference

4

Surgical incision healing and scar mobility evaluation

5

Gait analysis with or without assistive devices

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Early rehabilitation follows the surgeon's instructions for swelling management and comfortable movement

Progressive mobility and strengthening guided by symptoms, function, and the treating team's plan

Walking and daily-activity practice, with mobility aids used as advised by the treating team

Further strengthening and activity progression when appropriate for the person's recovery

Manual scar tissue mobilization and joint mobilizations as needed

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Perform ankle pumps and quadriceps sets every hour while awake to prevent blood clots

- Elevate the operated leg above heart level when resting to reduce swelling

- Apply ice packs for 15-20 minutes after exercise sessions

- Perform prescribed heel slides and knee bends 3 to 4 times daily

- Never place a pillow directly under the knee when resting—place it under the calf

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Follow the surgeon's instructions about when to start rehabilitation and which precautions apply. Contact the treating team if pain, swelling, wound changes, or mobility concerns worsen.
Schedule Assessment Today

Sports, Post-Op & GeneralService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Post-Surgical Rehabilitation ?

Post-surgical rehabilitation may support movement and daily activities after an operation. The appropriate exercises, precautions, and timeline depend on the procedure, healing, and instructions from the surgeon or hospital team. At Dr Hamid’s Physio and Pain Clinic in Manikonda, care is planned around the person's assessment and medical guidance; physiotherapy does not replace post-operative medical follow-up.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

A physiotherapist can review the surgeon's restrictions and help plan suitable mobility, strength, and walking activities as recovery progresses. Exercises and hands-on care depend on the operation and the individual's symptoms. Progress varies, and the treating surgical team should guide post-operative precautions and any changes in symptoms.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Post-operative immobilization causing rapid muscular atrophy and capsular adhesions

- Surgical trauma leading to persistent joint effusion and arthrogenic muscle inhibition (AMI)

- Formation of dense, fibrous surgical scar tissue restricting normal tendon gliding

- Compensatory altered gait mechanics developed prior to surgery during months of pre-op pain

- Loss of joint proprioception and sensorimotor feedback following surgical intervention

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Marked stiffness and severe restriction in active joint range of motion post-surgery

- Persistent post-operative swelling, warmth, and surgical incision site tightness

- Significant muscle wasting and weakness in the surgical limb (e.g. inability to perform a straight leg raise)

- Fear of weight-bearing and severe apprehension during initial walking attempts

- Difficulty navigating stairs, getting in and out of bed, or performing self-care independently

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Comprehensive review of surgical discharge summary, operative notes, and post-op X-rays

2

Inspection of surgical incision healing, surgical wound integrity, and skin mobility

3

Goniometric measurement of operative joint flexion and extension limits against surgical milestones

4

Circumferential measurement of limb girth to track swelling resolution and muscle mass

5

Gait pattern evaluation, assistive device fitting (walker/crutches/cane), and transfer safety check

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Circulatory and lymphatic pumping exercises alongside cryotherapy to clear post-op edema

Gentle passive and active-assisted range of motion maneuvers adhering to surgical range restrictions

Neuromuscular Electrical Stimulation (NMES) to overcome arthrogenic quad/rotator cuff inhibition

Manual scar tissue mobilization once incisions are fully healed to restore tissue extensibility

Progressive closed-kinetic-chain strengthening, balance retraining, and independent walking progression

Recovery and progress

Recovery timelines vary by surgery, healing, general health, and the surgeon's restrictions. Some procedures require several months of gradual rehabilitation. Follow the treating team's milestones rather than a fixed timetable.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Strictly perform your prescribed bedside ankle pumps and quad sets every 2 hours while awake

- Elevate the operated limb above heart level when resting to reduce dependent gravity edema

- Keep surgical incisions clean, dry, and protected until surgical sutures or staples are removed

- Never rush beyond surgical weight-bearing guidelines without explicit clinical clearance

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Post-surgical physiotherapy should typically commence within 24 to 72 hours after discharge or as explicitly recommended by your orthopedic surgeon. Contact Dr. Hamid immediately if you notice severe joint stiffness, worsening swelling, or struggle to bear prescribed weight safely.
Schedule Assessment Today

Specialized clinical rehabilitation for rotator cuff tears, tendonitis, impingement, and shoulder weakness.

Call +91 76010 26596 Chat on WhatsApp

![Rotator cuff physiotherapy and shoulder tendon treatment in Manikonda clinic](https://www.drhamidphysio.in/images/services/condition-shoulder-pain.webp)

ShoulderService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Rotator Cuff Physiotherapy ?

The rotator cuff is a group of muscles and tendons around the shoulder. Problems affecting this area can cause pain or weakness, including during reaching or lifting. Symptoms can have different causes; assessment may help discuss care options. Physiotherapy cannot guarantee that surgery will be avoided or that full function will return.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

Care may include gradual movement and strengthening, activity advice, or other options depending on the assessment and goals. Progress and response vary, and treatment cannot guarantee tendon healing or that surgery will not be needed.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Repetitive overhead activities in sports (badminton, tennis, swimming, cricket) or occupations

- Age-related tendon degeneration and reduced blood supply after age 40

- Subacromial impingement from bone spurs or thickened bursa compressing the tendons

- Poor scapular mechanics and rounded shoulder posture reducing subacromial space

- Acute trauma from falls onto an outstretched arm or heavy lifting

- Muscle imbalances between the deltoid and rotator cuff causing superior humeral head migration

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Pain on the outside or front of the shoulder, particularly when reaching overhead or behind the back

- Painful arc between 60-120 degrees of arm elevation

- Night pain and difficulty sleeping on the affected shoulder

- Weakness when lifting objects or rotating the arm against resistance

- Clicking, popping, or catching sensations during shoulder movement

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Empty Can (Jobe's) and Full Can tests to isolate supraspinatus function

2

External rotation and internal rotation strength testing against resistance

3

Neer's and Hawkins-Kennedy impingement provocative tests

4

Scapular dyskinesis assessment evaluating upward rotation and posterior tilt

5

Cervical spine screening to rule out referred pain from neck issues

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Pain relief phase: Gentle joint mobilizations, electrotherapy, and activity modification

Scapular stabilization exercises (serratus anterior wall slides, lower trapezius Y-raises)

Progressive rotator cuff strengthening using resistance bands at various angles

Posterior capsule stretching and thoracic extension exercises to improve posture

Functional retraining for overhead activities and return to sport or work

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Avoid sleeping on the painful shoulder; sleep on your back or unaffected side with a pillow under the arm

- Apply ice packs for 15 minutes after activities that provoke shoulder pain

- Avoid repetitive overhead activities and heavy lifting during the acute phase

- Perform gentle pendulum exercises daily to maintain joint mobility

- Maintain upright posture with shoulders back and down during desk work

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Seek assessment if shoulder pain persists beyond one week, prevents overhead activities or sleeping, or if you experience sudden weakness after an injury. Early treatment prevents progression to tears.
Schedule Assessment Today

# Runner's Knee Physiotherapy in Manikonda, Hyderabad

Specialized clinical rehabilitation for patellofemoral pain syndrome, anterior knee pain, and running-related knee injuries.

Call +91 76010 26596 Chat on WhatsApp

📍 Opp: HDFC Bank ATM, near Friends Colony Park, Puppalguda, Manikonda. Contact the clinic to ask about appointment availability.

![Runner's knee physiotherapy and patellofemoral pain treatment in Manikonda clinic](https://www.drhamidphysio.in/images/services/condition-knee-pain.webp)

KneeService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Runner's Knee Physiotherapy ?

Patellofemoral pain refers to pain around or behind the kneecap. It can be associated with running, squatting, stair climbing, or prolonged sitting, but causes vary and are not always explained by kneecap tracking alone. An assessment can help discuss suitable activity changes and care options.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

Care for pain around the kneecap may include a movement assessment, exercises, activity adjustments, or other options depending on the person's symptoms and goals. Taping may be considered in some cases, but its effect varies. A clinician can help plan a gradual return to activity.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Weakness in the vastus medialis obliquus (VMO) allowing lateral patellar tracking

- Hip abductor and external rotator weakness causing dynamic knee valgus during running

- Tight iliotibial band (ITB), hamstrings, or hip flexors increasing lateral patellar forces

- Training errors including rapid increases in mileage, hill running, or hard surface training

- Poor foot biomechanics such as overpronation causing excessive tibial internal rotation

- Improper running shoes or worn-out footwear lacking adequate support

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Gradual onset of pain around or behind the kneecap during or after running

- Pain when climbing or descending stairs, particularly going downhill

- Discomfort when sitting with knees bent for prolonged periods (movie theater sign)

- Crepitus or grinding sensation when bending and straightening the knee

- Mild swelling around the kneecap and tenderness along the patellar edges

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Running gait analysis to identify biomechanical faults, cadence, and foot strike pattern

2

Single-leg squat and step-down test to evaluate dynamic knee valgus and hip control

3

Patellar tracking, glide, and tilt assessment in weight-bearing and non-weight-bearing positions

4

Flexibility testing of ITB, hamstrings, hip flexors, and gastrocnemius

5

Hip abductor and external rotator strength testing comparing both sides

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Patellar taping may be considered where appropriate; response varies

Targeted hip strengthening (gluteus medius, maximus, and external rotators)

VMO-specific strengthening exercises to balance patellar tracking forces

ITB, hamstring, and hip flexor stretching and foam rolling program

Running form correction, cadence optimization, and gradual return-to-run program

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Consider adjusting running volume, hills, or speed while symptoms are active; seek individual guidance if unsure

- Apply ice packs for 15 minutes after runs to control inflammation

- Perform prescribed hip strengthening exercises daily

- Consider a temporary switch to cycling or swimming to maintain fitness

- Replace running shoes every 500-600 kilometers or when cushioning feels flat

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Consult Dr. Hamid if knee pain has persisted for more than a week despite rest, prevents you from running your normal distance, or recurs whenever you increase your training volume.
Schedule Assessment Today

# Sciatica Physiotherapy in Manikonda, Hyderabad

Targeted treatment for sciatic nerve pain, radiating leg pain, tingling, numbness, and disc-related sciatica. Includes assessment, nerve mobility work, and progressive rehabilitation.

Call +91 76010 26596 Chat on WhatsApp

📍 Opp: HDFC Bank ATM, near Friends Colony Park, Puppalguda, Manikonda. Contact the clinic to ask about appointment availability.

![Sciatica physiotherapy and sciatic nerve decompression in Manikonda clinic](https://www.drhamidphysio.in/images/services/condition-back-pain.webp)

Spine & BackService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Sciatica Physiotherapy ?

Sciatica is nerve pain caused by irritation, inflammation, or mechanical compression of the sciatic nerve — the largest nerve in the human body. The pain originates in the lower lumbar spine or buttock and radiates down through the back of the thigh, calf, and into the foot. At Dr Hamid’s Physio and Pain Clinic in Manikonda, we pinpoint the exact anatomical site of sciatic nerve entrapment — whether from a lumbar disc herniation, spinal canal narrowing, or piriformis muscle impingement.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

Sciatica physiotherapy focuses on neural decompression, nerve desensitization, and addressing the mechanical source of compression. Through specific neural mobilization (neurodynamic sliders and tensioners), Dr. Mohammed Hamid Ali restores smooth gliding of the sciatic nerve along its anatomical pathway while relieving mechanical disc pressure through directional extension and pelvic alignment.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Herniation or protrusion of the L4-L5 or L5-S1 lumbar intervertebral disc compressing the nerve root

- Piriformis syndrome, where a tight piriformis muscle in the buttock compresses the passing sciatic nerve

- Lumbar canal stenosis causing neural narrowing around the exiting nerve roots

- Degenerative disc disease leading to reduced neuroforaminal space in the lumbar spine

- Sacroiliac joint dysfunction creating compensatory pelvic torsion and neural irritation

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Electric shock-like, burning, or shooting pain radiating from the lower back or buttock down the leg

- Persistent numbness, tingling ('pins and needles') in the calf, heel, or toes

- Pain that worsens significantly upon prolonged sitting, coughing, or sneezing

- Weakness or heaviness in the affected leg making normal walking or toe-standing difficult

- Difficulty standing up straight or finding a comfortable sleeping posture

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Straight Leg Raise (SLR) and Slump neurodynamic tests to assess sciatic nerve sensitivity

2

Detailed dermatomal sensory mapping and myotomal motor power evaluation (L4, L5, S1)

3

Differential testing between lumbar disc radiculopathy and piriformis syndrome

4

Spinal range of motion and directional preference assessment to find pain-relieving postures

5

Gait analysis to detect antalgic limping or subtle foot drop

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Neural mobilization techniques to restore physiological excursion of the sciatic nerve

Directional extension therapy (McKenzie protocol) to centralize radiating leg symptoms

Targeted deep gluteal and piriformis manual soft tissue release

Gentle lumbar decompression traction and anti-inflammatory electro-modalities in acute flare-ups

Progressive lumbo-pelvic stabilization exercises to protect the nerve root from re-compression

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Avoid sitting on soft, deep couches that force your lower spine into prolonged flexion

- Place a supportive pillow under your knees when sleeping on your back, or between your knees when on your side

- Never push through intense shooting nerve pain during home stretches

- Perform gentle sciatic nerve gliding exercises strictly as demonstrated by Dr. Hamid

- Apply ice packs to the lower back/upper buttock for 15 minutes to reduce acute nerve root inflammation

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Consult Dr. Hamid promptly if shooting pain extends past your knee, your foot feels numb or heavy, or walking becomes difficult. Immediate emergency hospital evaluation is required if you experience loss of bowel or bladder control.
Schedule Assessment Today

ShoulderService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Shoulder Pain Physiotherapy ?

Shoulder pain can affect reaching, dressing, or sleeping and may have several causes. A clinical assessment can help consider possible contributors and whether physiotherapy or another type of care may be appropriate. Symptoms do not always identify the source by themselves.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

For shoulder pain, an individual physiotherapy plan may include activity advice and progressive shoulder exercises to support movement and function. Hands-on techniques may be considered when appropriate. The plan depends on the assessment, and improvement varies from person to person.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Subacromial impingement syndrome where the supraspinatus tendon is pinched under the acromion

- Rotator cuff tendinopathy or partial micro-tears from repetitive overhead lifting or sports

- Subacromial or subdeltoid bursitis causing sharp lateral shoulder inflammation

- Poor scapulothoracic rhythm (scapular dyskinesis) and rounded shoulder posture

- Biceps tendinitis affecting the long head of the biceps in the bicipital groove

- Sudden jarring pull or fall onto an outstretched hand (FOOSH injury)

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Pain and weakness when lifting your arm sideways or reaching overhead (the 'painful arc' between 60-120°)

- Deep, throbbing ache on the outside or front of the shoulder that worsens at night

- Inability to comfortably sleep on the affected shoulder

- Difficulty reaching behind your back to tuck in a shirt or fasten clothing

- Clicking, popping, or catching sensations during arm rotation

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Neer's and Hawkins-Kennedy impingement provocative tests

2

Empty Can (Jobe's) test and Full Can test to isolate the supraspinatus tendon

3

External and internal rotation isometric strength testing against resistance

4

Scapular dyskinesis testing evaluating winging and rhythmic upward rotation during arm elevation

5

Screening of the cervical spine to rule out referred C5-C6 radicular pain

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Glenohumeral posterior and inferior joint mobilizations to enlarge the subacromial space

Soft tissue release of tight pectoralis minor, levator scapulae, and posterior capsule

Progressive rotator cuff strengthening using elastic resistance bands at various angles

Scapular stabilization exercises (serratus anterior wall slides, lower trapezius Y-raises)

Ergonomic sleeping modification and functional reach pacing advice

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Avoid lifting heavy weights overhead or behind your back during the acute pain phase

- Perform gentle Codman's pendulum swings 3 times daily to relax shoulder muscles

- Sleep on your back or unaffected side with a pillow tucked under the painful arm for support

- Apply ice packs for 15 minutes after exercise or physical activity to reduce inflammation

- Maintain upright posture with shoulders relaxed back and down

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Consult Dr. Hamid if shoulder pain prevents sleeping, lasts longer than 7 days, or makes lifting your arm overhead painful.
Schedule Assessment Today

ShoulderService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Shoulder Rehabilitation ?

Shoulder Rehabilitation is an advanced, protocol-guided physical therapy program tailored for patients recovering from major shoulder surgery, anterior dislocations, Labral/Bankart lesions, SLAP tears, or proximal humerus fractures. Because the shoulder sacrifice bony stability for multi-planar mobility, rehabilitation must systematically restore active dynamic stabilization. At Dr Hamid’s Physio and Pain Clinic in Manikonda, Hyderabad, Dr. Mohammed Hamid Ali leads you safely through phased surgical protocols — protecting healing repairs while systematically rebuilding overhead strength, joint proprioception, and throwing/lifting capability.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

Our structured shoulder rehabilitation adheres strictly to biological tissue healing phases. In early phases, Dr. Mohammed Hamid Ali uses gentle passive range of motion to prevent arthrofibrosis without placing tension on surgical anchors. Once biological tendon-to-bone or labral healing is secure, active-assisted exercises, closed-chain kinetic loading, dynamic rhythmic stabilization, and functional sport-specific training are systematically integrated.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Post-operative recovery following arthroscopic or open rotator cuff tendon repair

- Post-surgical rehabilitation after Bankart repair, Latarjet procedure, or SLAP repair

- Rehabilitation following acute anterior or posterior glenohumeral dislocation/subluxation

- Post-fracture stiffness following surgical fixation of proximal humerus or clavicle fractures

- Severe multidirectional shoulder instability (MDI) and hypermobility syndrome

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Severe joint stiffness, scar tissue adhesions, and guarding after weeks in a shoulder immobilizer/sling

- Profound muscular atrophy of the deltoid, rotator cuff, and periscapular stabilizers

- Apprehension, vulnerability, or fear that the shoulder will 'pop out' during abduction and external rotation

- Inability to lift objects, drive, or return to recreational sports and fitness activities

- Persistent ache around the surgical portals or anterior joint capsule

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Verification of orthopedic surgical operative report, anchor locations, and immobilization guidelines

2

Passive range of motion measurement strictly respecting surgical safety parameters

3

Apprehension and Relocation tests for post-dislocation instability cases

4

Scapular rhythm, posture, and cervical spine screening

5

Strength testing of periscapular stabilizers (serratus anterior, rhomboids, trapezius)

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Phase 1: Sling weaning, passive forward flexion in scapular plane, and gentle pendular exercises

Phase 2: Active-assisted range of motion with wand/pulley, scapular retractions, and isometric rotator cuff setting

Phase 3: Active range of motion, closed-chain quadruped weight-bearing, and light resistance band strengthening

Phase 4: Rhythmic stabilization, pertubation training on stability balls, and dynamic rotator cuff endurance

Phase 5: Plyometrics, throwing/overhead athletic drills, and return-to-sport functional clearance

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Wear your prescribed shoulder abduction sling exactly as instructed by your surgeon until cleared

- Perform daily passive pendular exercises and wrist/hand pump exercises to maintain blood flow

- Never push into painful extension or external rotation past your surgeon's current limits

- Sleep in a semi-reclined position with a supportive pillow behind the elbow for comfort

- Keep all surgical portal sites clean and dry per post-op instructions

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Begin rehabilitation as soon as scheduled by your orthopedic surgeon (often starting with gentle passive motion at 2-3 weeks post-op). Home visits can be arranged in Manikonda and Puppalguda.
Schedule Assessment Today

Spine & BackService information

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Spinal Injuries Rehabilitation ?

Spinal injuries — resulting from motor vehicle accidents, domestic falls, sports trauma, or osteoporotic compression fractures — require careful, protocol-driven clinical rehabilitation. Whether recovering from a conservative period of spinal bracing (such as a Taylor's or TLSO brace) or post-surgical internal stabilization, restoring spinal confidence, segmental mobility, and muscular endurance is critical. At Dr Hamid’s Physio and Pain Clinic in Manikonda, Dr. Mohammed Hamid Ali provides safe, structured spinal rehabilitation that rebuilds functional independence step by step.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

Spinal injury rehabilitation adheres strictly to orthopedic healing timelines. Once bony consolidation is confirmed, Dr. Mohammed Hamid Ali guides patients through gentle active-assisted range of motion, gradual weaning from external braces, isometric muscle activation, and progressive kinetic chain strengthening. This carefully controlled loading promotes bone remodeling and restores confident daily movement.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Motorcycle, car, or pedestrian traffic accidents causing sudden spinal deceleration trauma

- Falls from heights or domestic slip-and-fall injuries resulting in stable vertebral fractures

- Osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in elderly individuals

- Severe sports collisions or violent hyperextension/hyperflexion trauma

- Post-surgical recovery following spinal fusion, discectomy, or laminectomy

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Localized vertebral tenderness and guarded spinal posture following trauma

- Severe muscular atrophy and stiffness following weeks of immobilization in a brace

- Fear of bending, rotating, or lifting even lightweight objects

- Loss of upright postural endurance, with early fatigue when standing or sitting

- Reduced thoracic chest expansion and compensatory neck or hip stiffness

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Thorough review of radiographic imaging (X-rays, CT, MRI) and orthopedic surgeon clearance

2

Gentle evaluation of protected spinal range of motion within prescribed safe limits

3

Postural and breathing mechanics evaluation following prolonged brace wear

4

Comprehensive neurological examination to verify nerve root and cord integrity

5

Functional balance, sit-to-stand, and walking tolerance assessment

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Gradual weaning protocols from TLSO, Taylor, or lumbar braces

Gentle thoracic expansion and diaphragmatic breathing restoration

Submaximal isometric spinal stabilization exercises in neutral alignment

Progressive kinetic chain strengthening of gluteal, hip, and shoulder girdle musculature

Functional retraining for safe daily activities (getting in/out of bed, chairs, cars)

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Wear your prescribed spinal brace exactly according to orthopedic instructions until cleared

- Log-roll when getting in and out of bed to prevent rotational strain on the healing spine

- Avoid all heavy lifting, sudden twisting, or high-impact jarring activities

- Perform gentle ankle pumps and deep breathing exercises daily to promote circulation

- Ensure walking pathways at home are free of loose rugs and trip hazards

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Begin rehabilitation as soon as cleared by your orthopedic or spine surgeon for physical therapy. Home visits can be arranged in Manikonda and Puppalguda.

Spine & BackService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Spine Physiotherapy & Rehabilitation ?

The human spine functions as an integrated kinetic chain. A restriction or misalignment in the thoracic spine or pelvis inevitably creates compensatory overload in the cervical or lumbar regions. Spine Physiotherapy at Dr Hamid’s Physio and Pain Clinic in Manikonda, Hyderabad takes a holistic, whole-spine approach. Rather than treating isolated pain spots, Dr. Mohammed Hamid Ali evaluates the global sagittal alignment, rib cage mechanics, pelvic levelness, and deep axial musculature to restore lasting spinal harmony.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

Whole-spine physiotherapy combines articular mobilization, myofascial release, and neuromuscular re-education. Dr. Mohammed Hamid Ali mobilizes stiff segments (frequently the thoracic spine), retrains diaphragmatic breathing, and activates deep stabilizing slings (anterior and posterior oblique slings) that hold your spine erect effortlessly without fatigue.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Chronic desk-bound postural fatigue creating thoracic kyphosis and compensatory forward head posture

- Idiopathic or postural scoliosis causing asymmetrical spinal loading

- Degenerative disc disease spanning multiple cervical and lumbar levels

- Sacroiliac joint dysfunction altering pelvic foundation mechanics

- General spinal deconditioning and lack of regular multi-planar mobility

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Generalized fatigue and aching along the length of the spine after standing or sitting

- Restricted trunk rotation when driving or looking over your shoulder

- Uneven shoulder heights, winged scapulae, or pelvic tilt

- Shallow breathing due to stiff thoracic facet and costovertebral joints

- Recurrent episodic flare-ups of both neck and lower back discomfort

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Global spinal postural plumb line analysis in multiple planes

2

Segmental assessment of cervical, thoracic, and lumbar mobility

3

Assessment of costovertebral joint excursion and chest expansion

4

Pelvic obliquity, leg length, and sacroiliac joint mobility testing

5

Evaluation of functional movement patterns (overhead squat, rotation, lateral bend)

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Thoracic spine extension and rotation mobilizations to unlock the mid-back

Myofascial release of tight pectoral, suboccipital, and hip flexor muscle groups

Neuromuscular re-education of deep postural erector spinae and scapular retractors

Functional multi-planar core stability exercises integrating upper and lower body

Personalized daily mobility routine and ergonomic workstation configuration

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Perform daily thoracic foam roller extensions or rolled-towel chest openers

- Incorporate the cat-camel stretch and thread-the-needle rotation daily

- Take micro-breaks from desk work every 40 minutes to walk and reset posture

- Engage in diaphragmatic deep breathing for 5 minutes daily to mobilize rib joints

- Use an ergonomic workstation with screen at eye level and supportive chair

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Book an appointment if you experience persistent spinal stiffness, postural fatigue, or recurrent episodes of neck and back ache.
