# Spondylolisthesis Physiotherapy in Manikonda, Hyderabad

Specialized clinical rehabilitation for vertebral slippage, spinal instability, and nerve compression from spondylolisthesis.

Call +91 76010 26596 Chat on WhatsApp

📍 Opp: HDFC Bank ATM, near Friends Colony Park, Puppalguda, Manikonda. Contact the clinic to ask about appointment availability.

![Spondylolisthesis physiotherapy and vertebral slip rehabilitation in Manikonda clinic](https://www.drhamidphysio.in/images/services/condition-back-pain.webp)

Spine & BackService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Spondylolisthesis Physiotherapy ?

Spondylolisthesis is a spinal condition where one vertebra slips forward over the vertebra below it, most commonly occurring at the L4-L5 or L5-S1 levels. This forward slippage can narrow the spinal canal, compress nerve roots, and cause persistent lower back pain, hamstring tightness, and radiating leg symptoms. The condition ranges from Grade I (mild, less than 25% slippage) to Grade V (complete displacement). At Dr Hamid’s Physio and Pain Clinic in Manikonda, Hyderabad, we provide specialized conservative management for stable spondylolisthesis, focusing on core stabilization, spinal decompression, and functional strengthening to avoid or delay surgical intervention.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

Conservative physiotherapy is highly effective for stable Grade I and II spondylolisthesis. Dr. Mohammed Hamid Ali implements a flexion-biased stabilization program that reduces shear forces on the slipped vertebra. Core bracing exercises, posterior pelvic tilt training, and neutral spine mechanics protect the unstable segment while strengthening the muscular corset that supports your spine during daily activities.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Degenerative changes in the discs and facet joints leading to segmental instability

- Spondylolysis (stress fracture in the pars interarticularis) from repetitive hyperextension in athletes

- Congenital vertebral defects affecting the structural integrity of the posterior elements

- Age-related weakening of spinal ligaments and supporting musculature

- Repetitive heavy lifting, high-impact sports, or occupational spinal stress over decades

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Persistent lower back ache that worsens with standing, walking, or arching backward

- Tightness in both hamstrings making it difficult to touch your toes

- Pain, numbness, or tingling radiating into the buttocks or legs (neurogenic claudication)

- Weakness or heaviness in the legs after walking short distances

- Pain relief when sitting or bending forward (shopping cart sign)

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Detailed review of standing lateral and flexion/extension X-rays to grade the slippage and assess stability

2

Segmental spinal stability testing and postural deviation analysis

3

Neurological examination including dermatomal sensory mapping, reflex testing, and myotomal strength

4

Hamstring flexibility and hip range of motion assessment

5

Functional walking tolerance and lumbar extension provocation testing

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Flexion-biased exercises (posterior pelvic tilts, bent-knee crunches) to reduce lumbar lordosis and shear stress

Deep core stabilization training targeting transversus abdominis and multifidus activation

Gentle neural mobilization to address associated nerve root irritation

Hamstring and hip flexor flexibility program to reduce posterior chain tension

Activity modification education and safe lifting mechanics training

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Avoid prolonged standing in excessive lumbar extension; maintain a slight posterior pelvic tilt

- Perform prescribed posterior pelvic tilt exercises 3 times daily

- Use a supportive chair with lumbar support set slightly higher than usual to encourage flexion

- Avoid high-impact activities, heavy deadlifts, and excessive backward bending

- Sleep on your side with knees bent or on your back with a pillow under the knees

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Consult Dr. Hamid if you have been diagnosed with spondylolisthesis, experience persistent back pain with leg symptoms, or have been advised to consider spinal surgery and want to explore conservative options first.

Sports, Post-Op & GeneralService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Sports Injury Rehabilitation ?

Sports injuries encompass acute traumas (such as ligament tears, muscle sprains, and joint dislocations) and chronic overuse syndromes (including stress fractures, shin splints, and tendonitis) sustained during athletic activity, gym workouts, or recreational sports. In dynamic sports-loving communities across Manikonda, Puppalguda, and Gachibowli, athletes frequently present with running injuries, badminton-related shoulder strains, cricket bowling stresses, and football ankle twists. At Dr Hamid’s Physio and Pain Clinic, sports rehabilitation bridges the gap between acute clinical recovery and peak athletic performance, focusing on tissue healing, kinetic chain re-alignment, and sport-specific reconditioning.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

Rehabilitation after a sports injury depends on the injury, symptoms, and sporting goals. After assessment, a plan may include activity adjustments, progressive strength and movement practice, and sport-specific work when appropriate. No plan can guarantee complete healing or prevent every recurrence.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Sudden explosive pivoting, jumping, or rapid deceleration without adequate muscular pre-activation

- Overuse and training errors such as sudden spikes in mileage or excessive weight progression at the gym

- Biomechanical imbalances including asymmetrical hip strength, foot overpronation, or poor core stability

- Inadequate warm-up, poor flexibility, and tight muscle chains restricting functional joint mobility

- Inadequate rest intervals and systemic recovery deficits leading to micro-trauma accumulation

- Playing on hard, irregular surfaces or wearing worn-out, unsupportive athletic footwear

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Sudden sharp pain during dynamic sporting movements, running, or heavy lifting

- Rapid swelling, joint effusion, or localized bruising at the site of trauma

- Instability, giving way sensation, or apprehension during lateral cutting motions

- Inability to bear full weight or generate explosive power through the injured limb

- Dull persistent post-workout ache and stiffness that lingers for days after exercise

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Detailed review of mechanism of injury, sporting demands, training volume, and equipment used

2

Selective tissue provocation testing (ligamentous stress tests, muscle tendon palpatory tests)

3

Range of motion goniometry and bilateral joint laxity evaluation

4

Kinematic screening of movement patterns (squatting, single-leg hopping, cutting mechanics)

5

Neuromuscular control, agility, and sport-specific force production measurement

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Early phase PRICE/PEACE & LOVE protocols with advanced electrotherapy to resolve swelling

Manual therapy, soft tissue release, and joint mobilizations to restore optimal joint glide

Targeted eccentric resistance training to rebuild collagen tensile strength in tendons and muscles

Proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation (PNF) and balance board training for joint stability

Progressive functional return-to-play protocols including running biomechanics and agility ladders

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Follow prescribed progressive loading rather than total passive immobilization

- Incorporate active dynamic warm-ups and post-workout static stretches into every routine

- Apply ice packs for 15-20 minutes following intense rehab drills to manage reactive swelling

- Prioritize 8 hours of restorative sleep and high-protein nutrition for optimal collagen synthesis

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Consult Dr. Hamid immediately if you experienced a distinct 'pop' sound during a sports move, cannot bear weight on the joint, observe rapid joint swelling within hours, or if persistent pain stops you from enjoying your favorite sport or workout.

# Stroke Physiotherapy in Manikonda, Hyderabad

Specialized clinical neuro-rehabilitation for post-stroke hemiplegia, paralysis, gait retraining, and upper limb functional recovery.

Call +91 76010 26596 Chat on WhatsApp

📍 Opp: HDFC Bank ATM, near Friends Colony Park, Puppalguda, Manikonda. Contact the clinic to ask about appointment availability.

![Stroke physiotherapy and neurological rehabilitation in Manikonda clinic](https://www.drhamidphysio.in/images/services/condition-neuro-rehab.webp)

Neurological & SpecialService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Stroke Physiotherapy & Rehabilitation ?

A stroke (cerebrovascular accident, CVA) occurs when blood flow to a part of the brain is interrupted by an ischemic clot or hemorrhage, resulting in neuronal cell damage. Patients frequently experience hemiplegia (paralysis of one side of the body), spasticity, loss of balance, facial weakness, and difficulty walking. Fortunately, the human brain possesses remarkable neuroplasticity — the ability to rewire surviving neural pathways through repetitive, meaningful practice. At Dr Hamid’s Physio and Pain Clinic in Manikonda, Hyderabad, Dr. Mohammed Hamid Ali provides specialized, compassionate neuro-rehabilitation that maximizes recovery potential and restores dignified functional independence.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

Neuro-rehabilitation utilizes task-specific training and neuroplastic stimulation. Dr. Mohammed Hamid Ali incorporates Bobath (NDT) principles, Motor Relearning Programmes (MRP), proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation (PNF), and constraint-induced movement techniques. Therapy systematically progresses from bed mobility and sitting balance to supported standing, symmetrical weight-bearing, and independent community ambulation.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Ischemic stroke caused by arterial thrombosis or embolism depriving brain tissue of oxygen

- Hemorrhagic stroke resulting from ruptured cerebral blood vessels or aneurysms

- Transient Ischemic Attacks (TIA) resulting in residual neuromuscular weakness

- Prolonged bed rest leading to joint contractures, muscle atrophy, and cardiovascular deconditioning

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Hemiparesis or hemiplegia (weakness or paralysis affecting the face, arm, and leg on one side)

- Spasticity and muscle tightness locking the elbow, wrist, fingers, or ankle into flexed positions

- Severe loss of balance, trunk control, and coordination making sitting or standing unsupported difficult

- Hemiplegic gait pattern characterized by hip circumduction and foot drop during walking

- Difficulty performing basic activities of daily living (bathing, dressing, feeding, transfers)

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Fugl-Meyer assessment of motor recovery and sensory impairment

2

Modified Ashworth Scale to quantify spasticity in flexor and extensor muscle synergies

3

Berg Balance Scale evaluating static and dynamic balance in sitting and standing

4

Functional Ambulation Category (FAC) to determine walking independence

5

Passive joint range of motion screening to identify early contractures in the shoulder and ankle

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Task-specific repetitive motor training targeting everyday functional movements

Inhibition techniques and prolonged passive stretching to manage spastic muscle groups

Trunk control and core stability exercises in sitting and bridging postures

Overground gait retraining with body-weight support, orthotic ankle bracing, and rhythmic auditory cues

Caregiver education on safe transferring techniques, positioning, and home exercise assistance

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Ensure proper hemiplegic arm positioning using pillows to prevent painful shoulder subluxation

- Follow the treating team's guidance on positioning and range-of-motion activity to maintain comfort and joint movement

- Encourage the patient to use their affected arm and leg in daily activities as much as possible

- Practice supported sit-to-stand repetitions from a firm chair 2-3 times daily

- Keep walking pathways at home free of loose rugs, wires, and furniture obstacles

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Begin stroke physiotherapy as soon as the patient is medically stable in the hospital or discharged home. Early intervention yields the highest neuroplastic gains. Home visits are available in Manikonda and nearby areas, generally targeted within an approximate 15 km radius of Manikonda; contact the clinic to confirm current coverage.
Schedule Assessment Today

# Tech Neck / Text Neck Physiotherapy in Manikonda, Hyderabad

Specialized clinical rehabilitation for forward head posture, device-related cervical strain, and postural neck dysfunction.

Call +91 76010 26596 Chat on WhatsApp

📍 Opp: HDFC Bank ATM, near Friends Colony Park, Puppalguda, Manikonda. Contact the clinic to ask about appointment availability.

![Tech neck physiotherapy and forward head posture correction in Manikonda clinic](https://www.drhamidphysio.in/images/services/condition-neck-pain.webp)

Neck & CervicalService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Tech Neck / Text Neck Physiotherapy ?

“Tech neck” or “text neck” is an informal phrase for neck or upper-back discomfort people associate with device use or sustained positions; it is not a medical diagnosis. Symptoms can have several causes, and no single posture explains every case. Assessment can help decide whether changes in activity or physiotherapy may be useful.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

For device-related neck discomfort, physiotherapy may include advice on varying positions, movement breaks, and exercises chosen for the person's symptoms and goals. The aim is to support comfortable activity, not to promise a permanent posture correction or prevent every recurrence.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Prolonged smartphone and tablet use with the head tilted forward and down

- Laptop and desktop monitor positioned below eye level encouraging forward head posture

- Weakness in deep cervical flexors and scapular stabilizers failing to support upright posture

- Tightness in suboccipital muscles, upper trapezius, and pectorals from sustained forward positioning

- Loss of the natural cervical lordosis (curve) from chronic postural stress

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Persistent dull ache across the base of the skull, neck, and tops of the shoulders

- Stiffness and reduced ability to turn the head fully while driving or checking blind spots

- Frequent tension headaches radiating from the upper neck to the temples or behind the eyes

- Rounded shoulders and visible forward head posture when viewed from the side

- Tight, tender muscle knots (trigger points) in the upper trapezius and between the shoulder blades

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Craniovertebral angle measurement using digital photography to quantify forward head posture

2

Deep neck flexor endurance testing (craniocervical flexion test)

3

Cervical and thoracic range of motion assessment in all planes

4

Palpation of suboccipital muscles, upper trapezius, and levator scapulae for trigger points

5

Assessment of scapular position, thoracic kyphosis, and pectoral muscle tightness

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Myofascial release of tight suboccipitals, upper trapezius, levator scapulae, and pectorals

Thoracic spine mobilization and extension exercises to open the chest and improve upright posture

Deep cervical flexor retraining (chin tucks and craniocervical flexion) to restore the natural cervical curve

Scapular retraction and stabilization exercises to support the shoulder girdle

Ergonomic workstation assessment and smartphone usage habit modification

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Raise your phone to eye level instead of tilting your head down to view the screen

- Position your laptop or monitor so the top third of the screen is at eye level

- Perform chin tucks every 30 minutes during device use: gently pull your chin straight back

- Take a 2-minute posture break every hour to stand, roll your shoulders back, and look up

- Sleep on your back with a cervical roll or contour pillow to support the natural neck curve

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Schedule an assessment if you experience daily neck stiffness and headaches from device use, notice rounded shoulders and forward head posture, or have persistent upper back tension that doesn't resolve with stretching.
Schedule Assessment Today

# Tendonitis Physiotherapy & Tendinopathy Care in Manikonda, Hyderabad

Specialized, progressive tendon loading therapy, collagen remodeling, and biomechanical correction for acute tendonitis and chronic tendinopathy in Manikonda.

Call +91 76010 26596 Chat on WhatsApp

📍 Opp: HDFC Bank ATM, near Friends Colony Park, Puppalguda, Manikonda. Contact the clinic to ask about appointment availability.

![Tendonitis physiotherapy and tendon rehabilitation in Manikonda clinic](https://www.drhamidphysio.in/images/services/exercise-therapy.webp)

Sports, Post-Op & GeneralService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Tendonitis Physiotherapy ?

Tendonitis (and its chronic counterpart, tendinopathy or tendinosis) is a painful musculoskeletal condition characterized by inflammation, micro-trauma, cellular disorganization, and degenerative breakdown of tendon tissue. Tendons are dense, fibrous connective bands that transmit mechanical force from skeletal muscles to bones. Common clinical presentations treated at Dr Hamid’s Physio and Pain Clinic in Manikonda include Achilles tendonitis (heel cord), Patellar tendonitis ('Jumper's knee'), Rotator Cuff tendonitis (shoulder), De Quervain's tenosynovitis (thumb/wrist), and Biceps tendonitis. Because tendons have low vascularity, conservative rest alone fails; tendons require scientifically calibrated mechanical loading to stimulate cellular collagen repair.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

Tendon rehabilitation has evolved dramatically: complete rest actually weakens tendons by inducing cellular catabolism. Tendons need load! Dr. Mohammed Hamid Ali implements modern Heavy Slow Resistance (HSR) and progressive eccentric loading protocols. Combined with targeted electrotherapy to reduce localized neurovascular ingrowth and pain, this structured loading stimulates tenocytes to produce healthy, organized Type I collagen, restoring the tendon's energy-storing spring capacity.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Sudden increases in training volume, running mileage, or repetitive workplace mechanical load

- Biomechanical movement faults causing abnormal shear and friction forces on the tendon

- Muscle stiffness and tightness in opposing muscle groups placing constant tensile strain on the tendon

- Inadequate rest periods between heavy workouts preventing cellular tendon matrix regeneration

- Age-related loss of tendon elasticity, ground substance changes, and poor micro-circulation

- Inappropriate footwear or unsupportive ergonomic equipment during repetitive activities

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Focal, well-localized pain directly over the tendon that is sharp during initial movement

- Characteristic 'morning tendon stiffness' that temporarily warms up with movement but aches severely afterward

- Palpable thickening, nodularity, or localized swelling along the tendon sheath

- Pain aggravated by explosive loading, jumping, uphill walking, or repetitive gripping

- Gradual loss of muscle power and endurance in the associated extremity

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Precise anatomical palpation and localized tendon provocation testing to isolate the affected structure

2

Classification of tendinopathy stage: reactive tendinopathy, tendon disrepair, or degenerative tendinopathy

3

Evaluation of adjacent joint mobility (e.g. ankle dorsiflexion in Achilles tendonitis; thoracic mobility in shoulder tendonitis)

4

Kinematic screening of functional tasks (squatting, jumping, heel raises, gripping)

5

Thorough review of training logs, weekly volume, running footwear, and workplace ergonomics

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Isometric loading drills (e.g. static wall sits, mid-range holds) providing immediate analgesia and tendon quietening

Therapeutic ultrasound and IFT to enhance micro-circulation and relieve acute peritendinous inflammation

Heavy Slow Resistance (HSR) and eccentric training to stimulate organized tenocyte collagen synthesis

Deep transverse friction massage and myofascial release along the associated muscle belly

Graduated energy-storage and plyometric reconditioning to restore sports-ready explosive springiness

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Perform your prescribed isometric holds (45-second static holds) whenever you feel tendon aches

- Avoid complete bed rest; keep walking within pain-free boundaries (pain should stay below 3/10)

- Wear supportive footwear with a slight heel raise (for Achilles issues) to reduce resting tendon tension

- Apply ice packs for 15 minutes following heavy loading sessions to control inflammatory flare-ups

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Schedule a consultation if you experience persistent morning tendon stiffness, feel a focal tender lump on your tendon, or notice that your tendon pain worsens day-by-day despite rest.
Schedule Assessment Today

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Tennis Elbow Physiotherapy ?

Tennis elbow, also called lateral elbow tendinopathy, can cause pain around the outside of the elbow, often with gripping or wrist activity. It can affect people who do and do not play tennis. Symptoms and contributing factors vary; an assessment can help discuss suitable care options.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

Care for tennis elbow may include activity modification and progressive exercises to support arm function. Some people may benefit from additional techniques, depending on assessment. Recovery and grip strength vary, so the plan should be reviewed as symptoms change.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Repetitive wrist extension and forceful gripping during computer mouse use, typing, or gaming

- Repeated manual twisting actions such as wringing clothes, opening tight jar lids, or turning screwdrivers

- Weight training errors such as excessive wrist extension during reverse curls, deadlifts, or pull-ups

- Racket sports with poor backhand technique transferring excessive vibration to the lateral elbow

- Micro-tears and failed collagen healing response (angiofibroblastic tendinosis) in the ECRB tendon

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Sharp, burning pain on the outer bony bump of the elbow that radiates down the forearm

- Marked weakness and sharp pain when lifting a coffee cup, kettle, or laptop with an outstretched arm

- Severe pain when shaking hands, turning a door handle, or wringing a towel

- Exquisite tenderness when pressing directly on the lateral epicondyle bone

- Morning stiffness in the elbow and forearm extensors

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Cozen's test: Resisted active wrist extension with the elbow extended and forearm pronated

2

Mill's test: Passive wrist flexion and pronation with elbow extended to stretch the ECRB tendon

3

Maudsley's test: Resisted extension of the middle finger isolating the ECRB tendon

4

Grip strength dynamometry comparing pain-free grip strength with the uninjured arm

5

Radial nerve neural tension testing to rule out radial tunnel syndrome

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Mulligan Mobilization with Movement (lateral glide to the elbow during pain-free gripping)

Deep transverse cross-friction massage over the ECRB tendon to stimulate fibroblast proliferation

Tyler Twist exercise protocol using flexible resistance bars (TheraBand flexbar)

Progressive eccentric wrist extensor loading (lowering weights slowly against gravity)

Prescription of a specialized counterforce brace worn 2-3 cm below the lateral epicondyle

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Lift everyday objects with your palm facing upwards (biceps-driven) rather than knuckles up

- Perform the prescribed eccentric Tyler Twist exercises twice daily

- Wear your counterforce tennis elbow strap during computer mouse work and lifting

- Apply ice packs for 12 minutes to the outer elbow after extended work sessions

- Avoid repetitive wrist-flicking movements during gym training or household tasks

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Schedule an assessment if elbow pain makes lifting coffee mugs painful, weakens your grip, or has persisted for more than two weeks.
Schedule Assessment Today

# TENS Therapy (Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation) in Manikonda

Non-invasive electrical nerve stimulation designed to block pain signals, stimulate natural endorphin release, and provide immediate pain modulation.

📍 Opp: HDFC Bank ATM, near Friends Colony Park, Puppalguda, Manikonda. Contact the clinic to ask about appointment availability.

![TENS therapy electrotherapy treatment session in Manikonda clinic](https://www.drhamidphysio.in/images/services/interferential-therapy.webp)

Supporting ModalitiesService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is TENS Therapy ?

Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) is a clinically proven, non-invasive electro-analgesic therapy used worldwide for acute and chronic pain management. TENS units deliver small, controlled electrical pulses through adhesive skin electrode pads positioned over or adjacent to painful nerves or dermatomes. By selectively stimulating large-diameter sensory nerve fibers (A-beta fibers), TENS triggers the Gate Control Mechanism in the dorsal horn of the spinal cord, effectively closing the neurological 'gate' and preventing pain signals from traveling up to the brain. Furthermore, low-frequency acupuncture-like TENS stimulates the pituitary gland to release the body's natural opiate-like pain relievers: endorphins and enkephalins. At Dr Hamid’s Physio and Pain Clinic in Manikonda, TENS serves as a safe, drug-free pain management tool.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

TENS offers an immediate, drug-free analgesic option without gastrointestinal or kidney side effects. Dr. Mohammed Hamid Ali tailors the pulse width, frequency, and electrode montage to your specific condition—using conventional high-frequency TENS (80–120 Hz) for immediate sensory pain-gating during active movement, or low-frequency burst TENS (2–10 Hz) for prolonged systemic endorphin release that lasts hours after treatment.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Acute post-surgical pain (following knee arthroscopy, abdominal surgery, or fracture repair)

- Diabetic peripheral neuropathy and post-herpetic neuralgia

- Chronic low back ache, neck tension, and myofascial pain syndrome

- Osteoarthritis flare-ups in knees, hips, and finger joints

- Tension-type headaches and temporomandibular joint (TMJ) discomfort

- Dysmenorrhea (painful menstrual cramping) and pelvic floor muscle soreness

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Sharp, shooting, or burning pain that prevents comfortable sleep or basic daily tasks

- Hypersensitive skin and nerve pathways that react intensely to minor contact

- Reliance on over-the-counter NSAIDs or pain pills that cause gastric acidity or drowsiness

- Difficulty performing early post-operative rehabilitation exercises due to surgical wound pain

- Chronic nerve-related aches that feel resistant to standard heating pads

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Accurate dermatomal mapping to identify the spinal nerve roots and peripheral nerve branches supplying the pain area

2

Selection of optimal TENS parameters (conventional sensory TENS vs motor acupuncture TENS)

3

Skin preparation and placement of hypoallergenic adhesive electrodes around the pain perimeter

4

Calibration of pulse width and amplitude based on patient sensory thresholds

5

Patient education on portable home TENS machine operation for safe personal pain control

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Electrode application over specific acupuncture points, trigger points, or along dermatomal lines

Gentle ramping of electrical amplitude until a distinct, comfortable 'prickling/buzzing' sensation is felt

20 to 30-minute treatment session while patient rests in an ergonomic position

Integration with gentle active range-of-motion drills during the therapeutic pain-suppression window

Prescription and training on home TENS devices for self-managed flare-ups when indicated

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Clean your skin with mild soap and water before applying TENS adhesive pads to ensure optimal conductivity

- Never place TENS pads over your carotid sinus (front of the neck), over broken skin, or over eyes

- Gradually increase amplitude until you feel strong but comfortable tingling; it should never feel painful

- Store electrode pads in a sealed plastic bag in a cool place to prolong adhesive gel life

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Schedule a session if you want drug-free pain relief for chronic joint aches, post-op soreness, or neuropathic pain, or if you need professional guidance on how to use a home TENS unit correctly.
Schedule Assessment Today

# Therapeutic Exercise Therapy in Manikonda, Hyderabad

Scientifically prescribed, individualized movement protocols designed to remediate physical impairments, restore muscular function, and optimize musculoskeletal health.

Sports, Post-Op & GeneralService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Therapeutic Exercise Therapy ?

Therapeutic exercise is the systematic, planned performance of specialized bodily movements, postures, and physical activities intended to remediate physical impairments, improve musculoskeletal and cardiovascular function, prevent complications, and optimize overall physical health. Unlike generic gym workouts, therapeutic exercise is a medical prescription: precise in dosage, vector, plane of movement, repetition count, and physiological loading. At Dr Hamid’s Physio and Pain Clinic in Manikonda, therapeutic exercise represents the cornerstone of long-term healing, transitioning patients from passive pain relief to active, resilient strength.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

Depending on the condition, physiotherapy may include education and an exercise plan that is progressed to the person's ability and goals. Some people may also use supportive treatments. No exercise or movement pattern can guarantee lifelong protection from injury or pain.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Post-injury muscular deconditioning and arthrogenic muscle inhibition

- Prolonged sedentary work lifestyles creating profound postural muscle imbalances

- Chronic joint stiffness resulting from lack of physiological movement and poor flexibility

- Inadequate core and spinal stabilizer strength failing to shield joints from routine physical loads

- Asymmetric muscular recruitment patterns developed after previous untreated sprains or fractures

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Rapid physical fatigue and muscle burning during modest everyday physical tasks

- Persistent joint stiffness and feeling 'locked' or tight upon waking or sitting

- Inability to maintain upright spinal posture without slouching or experiencing back ache

- Recurrent flare-ups of joint or tendon pain whenever attempting new physical activities

- Loss of functional movement ranges, such as reaching overhead or squatting down comfortably

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Comprehensive movement screening evaluating joint mobility, kinetic chain alignment, and stability

2

Manual Muscle Testing (MMT) and dynamometry to pinpoint focal muscular deficits

3

Postural and ergonomic assessment during static standing, sitting, and dynamic movement

4

Cardiovascular and muscular endurance evaluation benchmarked against age and lifestyle demands

5

Biomechanical movement flaw identification during squats, lunges, reaches, and overhead presses

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Range-of-motion and flexibility drills utilizing passive, active-assisted, and dynamic stretching

Targeted resistance training utilizing calibrated elastic bands, free weights, and bodyweight levers

Core and pelvic stabilization routines targeting transversus abdominis, multifidus, and gluteals

Neuromuscular re-education drills to re-establish proper motor unit firing patterns

Progressive functional task conditioning simulating work, sporting, and home physical demands

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Perform your prescribed exercise sets consistently at the recommended times each day

- Focus on slow, controlled eccentric and concentric phases rather than rushing repetitions

- Never push through sharp, stabbing joint pain; mild muscular fatigue and warmth are expected

- Stay well-hydrated and consume adequate protein to fuel muscular recovery and cellular repair

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Visit Dr. Hamid if you experience recurring aches whenever you exercise, struggle with chronic stiffness, are recovering from an injury, or want a personalized medical exercise plan to rebuild strength safely.

# Therapeutic Ultrasound Therapy in Manikonda, Hyderabad

High-frequency acoustic soundwave therapy stimulating deep tissue cellular repair, collagen synthesis, and rapid reduction of chronic inflammation.

📍 Opp: HDFC Bank ATM, near Friends Colony Park, Puppalguda, Manikonda. Contact the clinic to ask about appointment availability.

![Therapeutic ultrasound therapy treatment session in Manikonda clinic](https://www.drhamidphysio.in/images/services/ultrasound-therapy.webp)

Supporting ModalitiesService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Therapeutic Ultrasound ?

Therapeutic ultrasound is an established electro-physical modality that applies high-frequency sound waves (typically 1 MHz for deep tissues or 3 MHz for superficial structures) to injured biological tissues. Unlike diagnostic ultrasound used for imaging, therapeutic ultrasound transmits micro-vibrational acoustic energy deep into muscles, tendons, ligaments, and joint capsules. This produces both thermal effects (deep tissue warming, vasodilation, pain reduction) and non-thermal acoustic cavitation and microstreaming (accelerating cell membrane permeability, fibroblast proliferation, and cellular healing). At Dr Hamid’s Physio and Pain Clinic in Manikonda, ultrasound is expertly paired with active physical rehabilitation to supercharge tissue repair.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

While topical balms and superficial heating pads only penetrate a few millimeters of skin, therapeutic ultrasound penetrates up to 3 to 5 centimeters into dense connective tissues. Dr. Mohammed Hamid Ali applies an acoustic coupling gel and glides the soundhead in precise circular motions over the injured site. The acoustic micro-vibrations stimulate cell membrane metabolism, accelerate the synthesis of high-tensile Type I collagen, and break down fibrotic adhesions, preparing stiff tissues for painless manual stretching and strengthening.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Acute and chronic tendinopathies (Achilles tendonitis, patellar tendinopathy, rotator cuff irritation)

- Ligament sprains and post-traumatic joint capsule thickening (ankle sprains, wrist injuries)

- Dense fibrous post-surgical or post-injury scar tissue adhesions restricting joint range

- Plantar fasciitis and calcaneal heel spur irritation

- Deep chronic muscle spasm knots and myofascial trigger point inflammation

- Bursitis (subacromial bursitis, trochanteric hip bursitis)

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Focal, deep-seated tendon tenderness that fails to heal with simple rest

- Dense, puckered surgical scar tissue that feels tight, painful, or restricts stretching

- Sharp morning heel pain or Achilles tendon stiffness upon rising

- Persistent swelling and localized inflammatory fluid accumulation following a joint sprain

- Chronic ache in joints where superficial heat packs cannot penetrate deeply enough

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Clinical palpation to identify the exact depth, margin, and chronicity of injured tissue

2

Selection of optimal soundwave frequency (1 MHz for deep muscles/tendons; 3 MHz for superficial joints)

3

Duty cycle calibration (continuous mode for deep thermal heating; pulsed mode for acute inflammation)

4

Evaluation of patient sensory feedback and exclusion of contraindications (metal implants, fractures)

5

Baseline range-of-motion and pain scale documentation to track immediate post-session improvements

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Application of hypoallergenic conductive gel directly over the target treatment area

Continuous gentle circular motion of the ultrasound transducer head for 5 to 10 minutes

Pulsed mode settings used for acute sprains to stimulate cellular repair without creating tissue heat

Continuous mode settings applied for chronic joint contractures to soften tight collagen fibers

Immediate follow-up with targeted manual joint mobilization and active stretching while tissue is warm

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Drink a glass of water after ultrasound treatment to support cellular metabolic flushing

- Perform your prescribed gentle range of motion stretches within 2 to 3 hours after treatment

- Avoid applying direct ice immediately after continuous thermal ultrasound sessions

- Keep a log of tendon stiffness changes during your morning routine to share with Dr. Hamid

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Therapeutic ultrasound is ideal if you suffer from stubborn tendon pain (Achilles, tennis elbow, shoulder), thick surgical scars, or heel pain that has not responded to oral pain relievers.

# Vestibular Rehabilitation / Vertigo Physiotherapy in Manikonda, Hyderabad

Specialized clinical canalith repositioning maneuvers and vestibular adaptation therapy for BPPV, labyrinthitis, and chronic dizziness.

Call +91 76010 26596 Chat on WhatsApp

📍 Opp: HDFC Bank ATM, near Friends Colony Park, Puppalguda, Manikonda. Contact the clinic to ask about appointment availability.

![Vestibular rehabilitation and vertigo physiotherapy treatment in Manikonda clinic](https://www.drhamidphysio.in/images/services/condition-neuro-rehab.webp)

Neurological & SpecialService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Vestibular Rehabilitation / Vertigo Physiotherapy ?

Vertigo and balance disorders affect millions of people, causing terrifying sensations that the room is spinning violently, nausea, lightheadedness, and profound unsteadiness. The most common cause is Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV), where microscopic calcium carbonate crystals (otoconia) detach and become displaced into one of the semicircular canals of the inner ear. At Dr Hamid’s Physio and Pain Clinic in Manikonda, Hyderabad, Dr. Mohammed Hamid Ali provides specialized Vestibular Rehabilitation Therapy (VRT) and canalith repositioning maneuvers (such as the Epley maneuver) that frequently resolve BPPV vertigo completely in just 1 to 3 sessions.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

Vestibular physiotherapy works with remarkable precision. For BPPV, Dr. Mohammed Hamid Ali performs accurate diagnostic testing to determine which ear and canal are involved, followed immediately by gentle, evidence-based particle repositioning maneuvers (Epley, Semont, or BBQ roll) that use gravity to guide the loose crystals back to their safe home in the utricle. For chronic dizziness, vestibular adaptation and habituation exercises retrain the brain to process balance signals smoothly.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) with canalithiasis in the posterior or horizontal semicircular canal

- Vestibular neuritis or labyrinthitis following a viral inner ear infection

- Head trauma, whiplash, or sudden deceleration dislodging otoconia crystals

- Age-related degeneration of inner ear vestibular hair cells and otolithic membranes

- Cervicogenic dizziness originating from restricted upper cervical joint receptors (C1-C3)

- Persistent Postural-Perceptual Dizziness (PPPD) and sensory mismatch syndromes

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Violent, sudden spinning sensation (vertigo) triggered by rolling over in bed, looking up, or bending down

- Episodes of spinning lasting from 15 seconds to a couple of minutes accompanied by nausea

- Persistent floating, woozy, or lightheaded sensation when walking in busy environments (supermarkets, malls)

- Loss of balance and unsteadiness, feeling as though you are being pulled to one side

- Difficulty focusing eyes clearly when turning your head rapidly (oscillopsia)

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Dix-Hallpike test to assess the posterior semicircular canals and observe nystagmus

2

Supine Roll test to evaluate the horizontal semicircular canals

3

Vestibulo-Ocular Reflex (VOR) testing, including head thrust test and dynamic visual acuity

4

Romberg test, Sharpened Romberg, and Fukuda stepping test for postural balance

5

Cervical spine screening to differentiate inner ear vertigo from cervicogenic dizziness

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Canalith Repositioning Procedures (Epley maneuver, Semont maneuver, BBQ Roll)

Gaze stabilization exercises (VOR x1 and VOR x2 exercises) to eliminate visual blurring

Habituation exercises (Brandt-Daroff exercises) for motion-induced sensitivity

Dynamic balance retraining on firm and compliant foam surfaces with eyes open and closed

Gentle upper cervical manual therapy if cervicogenic dizziness is identified

Recovery and progress

Response and time to improvement vary. Some people with benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) improve after a clinician-guided repositioning procedure; other vestibular conditions may need a different assessment and rehabilitation plan.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Follow post-maneuver positioning instructions: keep head upright for the rest of the day

- Sleep with head slightly elevated on two pillows for the first 24-48 hours post-treatment

- Perform prescribed gaze stabilization (VOR) exercises smoothly 2-3 times daily

- Avoid rapid, extreme head-tilting movements immediately following repositioning

- Ensure bathroom and bedroom walkways are well-lit at night to prevent falls

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Schedule an assessment immediately if turning in bed, tilting your head up, or bending down triggers a violent spinning sensation. Seek urgent hospital emergency care if dizziness occurs with facial drooping, slurred speech, or arm weakness.
Schedule Assessment Today

Sports, Post-Op & GeneralService information

This page is general information. Suitability and progress depend on an individual assessment.

## Health information

This page provides general information and is not a diagnosis or individual treatment plan. Suitability and progress vary. Follow your treating clinician’s or surgeon’s instructions, especially after an injury or operation, and seek urgent medical care for sudden severe or concerning symptoms.

Clinical Overview & Definition

## What is Whiplash Injuries Physiotherapy ?

A whiplash injury (clinically termed Cervical Acceleration-Deceleration or CAD syndrome) is a traumatic injury to the cervical spine caused by rapid, violent forward-and-backward whipping motion of the head. Most frequently sustained during rear-end automobile collisions, bike skids, sporting impacts, or severe slips, whiplash strains cervical muscles, sprains anterior and posterior spinal ligaments, irritates facet joints, and can compress exiting cervical nerve roots. At Dr Hamid’s Physio and Pain Clinic in Manikonda, whiplash physiotherapy delivers gentle, evidence-based physical care that prevents acute post-accident neck trauma from becoming debilitating chronic pain.

### How Targeted Physiotherapy Restores Function

After whiplash, an appropriate plan depends on the injury and symptoms. A clinician may discuss comfortable movement and a gradual return to usual activities. Follow medical advice about collars, exercise, and activity, and seek assessment for worsening or concerning symptoms.

## Common Causes

Primary mechanical, postural, and physiological factors observed in our Manikonda clinic:

- Rear-end or side-impact motor vehicle collisions causing sudden acceleration-deceleration of the head

- Two-wheeler skids and sudden braking forcing the rider's neck through violent hyper-flexion and extension

- High-impact contact sports collisions (football, rugby, martial arts) or rollercoaster sudden jolts

- Severe slips and falls landing on back or buttocks, transmitting shock forces up into the cervical spine

- Secondary muscular guarding and sympathetic nervous system distress following acute vehicular trauma

## Frequent Symptoms

Signs and functional limitations indicating need for physical therapy:

- Neck pain and marked stiffness developing within 6 to 48 hours following the impact accident

- Inability to turn the head to look over shoulders while driving or crossing streets

- Suboccipital headaches starting at the base of the skull and radiating forward over the forehead

- Tenderness and rock-hard muscular spasms across the trapezius, levator scapulae, and rhomboids

- Shoulder and upper back aching, often accompanied by mild dizziness, jaw pain (TMJ), or arm tingling

Step-by-Step Clinical Assessment

## Our Diagnostic Evaluation in Manikonda

An assessment may include discussion of your symptoms and goals, plus movement checks selected for your individual needs.

1

Thorough screening using the Canadian C-Spine Rule to verify absence of cervical fractures or instability

2

Quebec Task Force classification of Whiplash-Associated Disorders (WAD Grade I, II, or III)

3

Gentle active cervical range of motion goniometry in all planes (flexion, extension, rotation, side bending)

4

Assessment of deep cervical flexor endurance (Craniocervical Flexion Test using biofeedback principles)

5

Palpation of cervical facet joints, suboccipital musculature, and neural tension screening for upper limbs

Multimodal Treatment Protocol

## Evidence-Based Treatment Approach

We integrate hands-on manual mobilizations, targeted electro-physical modalities, and progressive active exercise therapy:

Gentle electrotherapy (IFT/TENS) and moist heat packs to ease intense cervical paraspinal spasms

Gentle Grade I-II manual cervical mobilizations to restore hypomobile facet joint glide painlessly

Myofascial trigger point release and gentle suboccipital decompression to extinguish cervicogenic headaches

Craniocervical deep neck flexor retraining (chin tucks) to restore essential spinal postural stability

Postural re-education, scapular stabilization, and gentle return to normal driving and desk work

Recovery and progress

Recovery time and response vary with the diagnosis, symptom severity, overall health, treatment, and individual progress. An assessment can help set goals and review progress; no fixed timeline or outcome can be promised.

### Home Care & Ergonomics

- Avoid wearing a hard neck collar for more than 24-48 hours; gentle active movement accelerates healing

- Apply moist warmth or a warm neck wrap for 15 minutes before performing prescribed gentle chin tucks

- Adjust your car headrest so the middle of the headrest is level with the top of your ears

- Take frequent micro-breaks during computer work to avoid holding your neck in forward poking postures

### When to Consult Dr. Hamid

Consult Dr. Hamid within 48 to 72 hours of an accident. Seek emergency hospital care first if you experienced loss of consciousness, memory gaps, progressive arm weakness, or difficulty swallowing.
